scientific_question: Which occurrence/non-detection observations are exact falsifiers once imperfect detection and false-positive observation processes are made explicit?

observation_world.exact_compatibility: A biological state is compatible with an observation world when the exact observation history has probability > 0.

primary_hypotheses.claim: For every finite n and every p<1, an all-zero detection history remains possible when the species is truly present, so it cannot exactly falsify presence.
primary_hypotheses.rule: Any p<1,n case assigning zero probability to all-zero history under Z=1 refutes O1.

primary_hypotheses.claim: When p=1 and q=0, an all-zero history is impossible under presence and therefore is a valid exact negative witness.
primary_hypotheses.rule: Any n>=1 case retaining Z=1 after all-zero history under p=1 refutes O2.

primary_hypotheses.claim: For 0<p<1, increasing n reduces the probability of all-zero history under presence monotonically but never makes it impossible at finite n.
primary_hypotheses.rule: Any non-monotone increase or exact zero probability at finite n refutes O3.

primary_hypotheses.claim: A positive detection exactly falsifies absence only when every admissible observation world has q=0; if any admissible q>0, absence remains possible.
primary_hypotheses.rule: Any robust hard-positive claim with an admissible q>0 refutes O4.

primary_hypotheses.claim: Expanding the admissible observation-process universe cannot create a new robust hard falsification; it can only preserve or remove one.
primary_hypotheses.rule: Any expansion from a stricter to broader p/q universe that creates a robust hard exclusion refutes O5.

claim_boundary: Likelihood differences are not converted into arbitrary hard-falsification thresholds.
Exact falsification means zero probability under every admissible observation world.
Perfect detection is an idealized calibration condition, not assumed for real ecological surveys.
This protocol addresses observation-process identifiability, not ecological process truth.
